skill.name: baoyu-image-gen
skill.description: Generate images with OpenAI or Google APIs from prompts, prompt files, or reference images, with aspect ratio and quality controls.
skill.summary: Creates API-based images from prompts with provider, size, quality, and reference image options.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: The code mostly implements the documented image-generation workflow, and many static hits are documentation backticks or JavaScript template literals. Confirmed risks center on loading project and home env files, sending API credentials over network requests, and allowing project configuration to redirect provider base URLs.

remediation.issue: Project env files can set custom provider base URLs while API keys come from user or home configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for custom base URLs, or allow only official OpenAI and Google domains by default.

remediation.issue: The loader imports all keys from .baoyu-skills/.env into process.env.
remediation.suggestion: Whitelist only documented keys and separate project preferences from credential-bearing environment files.

remediation.issue: Provider requests send prompts, reference images, and API credentials to external endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Document network egress clearly and warn users before sending sensitive prompt files or reference images.

remediation.issue: Usage examples rely on npx -y bun without pinning the runtime package version.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned runtime version or a local executable path to reduce package-resolution supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Project Configuration Can Redirect API Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The script loads project .baoyu-skills/.env values, then uses OPENAI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_BASE_URL for requests that include API keys. A malicious project can set a custom endpoint and receive provider credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly loads cwd .baoyu-skills/.env into process.env and provider code uses base URL env vars for credentialed fetch calls.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Invocation Through npx
semantic_findings.description: The usage instructions invoke npx -y bun without a pinned package version. This can execute package-manager-resolved code before the local skill script runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command path is clear, but the practical risk depends on how the host environment resolves npx and bun.

content.user_title: Generate Images with OpenAI and Google
content.value_statement: Image prompts often need provider setup, sizes, and repeatable output paths. This skill runs an API-based generator with aspect ratio, quality, and reference image options.
actual_capabilities: Generates images from prompt text through OpenAI or Google APIs.
Reads prompts from direct text, stdin, or prompt files.
Supports common aspect ratios and OpenAI size mapping.
Accepts reference images for supported Google multimodal models.
Saves generated image bytes to a requested output path.
Can return JSON metadata with provider, model, and saved image path.
limitations: Requires a valid OpenAI, Google, or Gemini API key.
Reference images are only used with supported Google multimodal models.
Custom base URLs require careful trust because credentials are sent there.
The script saves only the first image found in provider responses.

use_cases.title: Create Design Drafts
use_cases.description: Generate concept art, product scenes, or campaign visuals from short prompts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Marketing Assets
use_cases.description: Create wide, square, or portrait images for posts, slides, and landing pages.

use_cases.title: Automate Visual Workflows
use_cases.description: Add API image generation to agent workflows with chosen providers and output paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Single Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baoyu-image-gen to create one image of a modern desk setup at sunrise. Save it as desk-scene.png.

prompt_templates.title: Set Shape and Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Control dimensions for a publishing channel
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 16:9 hero image for a productivity app. Use 2k quality and save it in the project assets folder.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provided reference image and generate a blue variant with the same composition. Use the Google provider.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Provider-Specific Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three options for a launch banner with OpenAI. Use a landscape aspect ratio and return concise result details.

output_examples.input: Prompt: A calm product background for a smartwatch, 16:9.
output_examples.output: A saved wide image path and a short confirmation naming the provider and model.

output_examples.input: Prompt files: brand brief and campaign theme. Output: social-card.png.
output_examples.output: A generated image file that combines both prompt files into one visual request.

output_examples.input: Reference image: source.png. Prompt: Make the object blue.
output_examples.output: A saved variation that uses the reference image when a supported Google model is selected.

best_practices: Keep API keys in user-level environment config and avoid committing project env files.
Use explicit output paths inside the current project.
Review custom base URLs before sending prompts or reference images.
anti_patterns: Do not use secret documents as prompt files or reference images.
Do not enable custom provider endpoints from untrusted projects.
Do not request large batches without checking API cost and rate limits.

faq.question: Which providers does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports OpenAI image generation and Google image models through API calls.

faq.question: Does it need API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Set OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, or GEMINI_API_KEY before running generation.

faq.question: Can it use reference images?
faq.answer: Yes, but reference images are only sent to supported Google multimodal models.

faq.question: Can I control image shape?
faq.answer: Yes. Use aspect ratio, size, quality, or Google image size options.

faq.question: Where are images saved?
faq.answer: Images are written to the output path supplied with the image option.

faq.question: Is custom endpoint support safe?
faq.answer: Only use custom base URLs that you trust because API credentials are sent to them.
